title: Banking Model Atlas
scenario: Maple Harbour Bank — a fictional Canadian retail bank
description: An original educational reference model for retail accounts and credit-card servicing. Not an operational bank schema.

domains.label: Customers
domains.description: Who banks with us and how we contact them.

domains.label: Bank and reference data
domains.description: Shared branch, channel and currency definitions.

domains.label: Products
domains.description: What the bank offers and which version was agreed.

domains.label: Accounts and credit
domains.description: Ownership, account lifecycle and credit limits.

domains.label: Cards
domains.description: Issued cards, their users and their lifecycle.

domains.label: Payments and statements
domains.description: Repayments, billing documents and balance snapshots.

domains.label: Disputes
domains.description: Customer claims and the progress of each case.

entities.label: Customer
entities.description: A person with a relationship to the fictional bank.

columns.description: Invented display name; never an actual customer name.

notes: Organizations and beneficial ownership are outside this version.

entities.label: Customer Address
entities.description: An address held for a customer over a period.
entities.grain: One customer address assignment for one purpose and interval.

columns.description: Stable synthetic identifier for customer address.
Person to whom this address belongs.
First invalid day, exclusive; null means open-ended.

notes: Overlapping addresses of the same purpose are disallowed in this fictional scenario.

entities.label: Customer Contact
entities.description: A way to reach a customer.
entities.grain: One contact method for a customer.

columns.description: Stable synthetic identifier for customer contact.
Fictional contact value; example emails use example.com.
Whether this is preferred within its contact type.

notes: Contact history and verification evidence are deferred.

entities.label: Customer Consent
entities.description: A recorded choice about a specific optional purpose.
entities.grain: One consent decision event for one customer and purpose.

columns.description: Stable synthetic identifier for customer consent.
Optional use covered by the choice.

notes: Latest event per customer and purpose defines the current choice. This is not a legal compliance implementation.

entities.label: Branch
entities.description: A servicing location or virtual branch.
notes: Virtual branch allows digital accounts without forcing a physical visit.

entities.label: Channel
entities.description: A route through which a customer action occurs.
notes: Channel describes origin, not a person or device.

entities.label: Currency
entities.description: A currency reference used by monetary entities.

columns.description: Currency code; CAD is the only supported value.
Number of fractional digits; 2 for CAD.

notes: Foreign exchange and cross-currency settlement are excluded.

entities.label: Product
entities.description: A named deposit or credit-card offering.

columns.description: Account family supported by this product.

notes: An account refers to a version, not directly to a mutable marketing description.

entities.label: Product Version
entities.description: A dated edition of product terms.

columns.description: Stable synthetic identifier for product version.
First day no longer offered, exclusive.

notes: Existing accounts retain their booked version after the offering closes. APR calculations are out of scope.

entities.label: Fee Type
entities.description: A category of account fee.

columns.description: Stable synthetic identifier for fee type.

notes: No fee engine or fee schedule is implemented.

entities.label: Account
entities.description: A customer-facing deposit or credit-card account.

columns.description: Product terms booked at account opening.

notes: Kind is derived through product_version and product. Account numbers are not stored.

entities.label: Account Holder
entities.description: Ownership or signing authority over an account.
entities.grain: One customer role on an account for an interval.

columns.description: Stable synthetic identifier for account holder.
Account to which the role applies.
Legal or operational role in this fictional scenario.

notes: Deposits can have joint owners. Credit-card accounts have one primary owner; supplementary card users are not account owners.

entities.label: Account Status Event
entities.description: A lifecycle change for an account.

columns.description: Stable synthetic identifier for account status event.

notes: The latest event defines current status; historical entries are not rejected using current status.

entities.label: Credit Facility
entities.description: The credit agreement attached to a credit-card account.

columns.description: Stable synthetic identifier for credit facility.
Credit-card account supported by this facility.
Must match the linked account currency.

notes: Exactly one facility for each credit-card account; none for deposit accounts. Loans and underwriting are excluded.

entities.label: Credit Limit Event
entities.description: A change in the approved credit limit.
entities.grain: One effective limit change per facility.

columns.description: Stable synthetic identifier for credit limit event.
UTC time from which the limit applies.
Nonnegative approved limit in facility currency.

notes: Latest effective event gives current limit. Available credit also needs holds and balances, so it is not calculated here.

entities.label: Card
entities.description: An issued credit-card instrument.
entities.grain: One issued card instance, including each replacement.

columns.description: Earlier card replaced by this card, when applicable.

notes: No PAN, CVV, PIN or magnetic-stripe data. Debit cards and digital tokens are deferred.

entities.label: Card Assignment
entities.description: The person authorized to use a card.

columns.description: Stable synthetic identifier for card assignment.

notes: A supplementary user need not own the account. A card has at most one assigned person at a time.

entities.label: Card Status Event
entities.description: A change in a card lifecycle.

columns.description: Stable synthetic identifier for card status event.

notes: Replacement does not move old transactions onto the new card.

entities.label: Merchant Category
entities.description: A fictional grouping for merchant analytics.

columns.description: Stable synthetic identifier for merchant category.
Display category such as groceries or travel.

notes: Codes are illustrative; no claim of a complete network MCC reference.

entities.label: Merchant
entities.description: A merchant identity observed in card activity.

columns.description: Country code; CA in this scenario.

notes: Merchant identity resolution across acquirers is deferred.

entities.label: Card Authorization
entities.description: A request to approve card spending before posting.

columns.description: Stable synthetic identifier for card authorization.

notes: An authorization is not a posted purchase. Hold expiry, incremental authorizations and reversals are deferred.

entities.label: Card Transaction
entities.description: A posted purchase or refund received through the card network.
entities.grain: One posted card purchase or refund.

columns.description: Stable synthetic identifier for card transaction.
Related authorization when available; may be absent for offline clearing.
Positive amount; kind determines economic direction.
Business date on which activity was posted.

notes: One authorization may support multiple posted presentments. The relationship does not imply equal amounts.

entities.label: Account Entry
entities.description: An immutable customer-account movement used for statement presentation.
entities.grain: One booked debit or credit on an account.

columns.description: Stable synthetic identifier for account entry.
Card activity behind this entry, if any.
Repayment behind this entry, if any.
Fee category when this is a fee.
Earlier entry reversed by this entry.

notes: These are account subledger-style entries, not a balanced general ledger. A separate rule defines balance signs by account kind.

entities.label: Payment
entities.description: An external repayment to a credit-card account.

columns.description: Payment currency; must match the account.

notes: All funding is external in this release. No internal transfer or payment-rail implementation.

entities.label: Statement
entities.description: An issued monthly billing snapshot for a credit-card account.
entities.grain: One issued statement for an account and cycle.

columns.description: Signed amount owed at start; negative means customer credit.
Nonnegative supplied amount; calculation is outside scope.

notes: Issued statements are immutable. Reissues and interest calculations are deferred.

entities.label: Statement Line
entities.description: A printed item on an issued statement.
entities.grain: One account entry displayed on one statement.

columns.description: Stable synthetic identifier for statement line.

notes: Amounts come from immutable entries. An entry appears on at most one issued statement in this simplified model.

entities.label: Account Balance Snapshot
entities.description: A supplied end-of-day account balance.

columns.description: Stable synthetic identifier for account balance snapshot.
Signed deposit funds or signed credit-card amount owed, according to account kind.

notes: A snapshot is a reconciliation reference, not a second source of transactions. Opening positions are required to rebuild balances.

entities.label: Dispute Reason
entities.description: A project-local category for customer claims.

columns.description: Stable synthetic identifier for dispute reason.

notes: Not a card-network reason-code catalogue.

entities.label: Dispute
entities.description: A customer claim about a posted purchase.
entities.grain: One dispute case against one purchase.

columns.description: Positive challenged portion of the purchase.
UTC time the case was opened.

notes: The owner or assigned card user may raise a case. A claim does not itself create a refund or provisional credit.

entities.label: Dispute Event
entities.description: A lifecycle event within a dispute case.

columns.description: Stable synthetic identifier for dispute event.
Synthetic operational note; no personal narrative.

notes: Chargeback messages, evidence files and provisional-credit postings are deferred.

rules.statement: An account opens within its product version offering interval and keeps that version; later product migration is deferred.
Every open account has exactly one active PRIMARY owner. JOINT roles are allowed only for deposit products; identical customer/account/role intervals must not overlap.
All validity intervals are [valid_from, valid_to); a non-null end is after the start. Address intervals for one customer/purpose do not overlap; card assignments for one card do not overlap.
Each credit-card account has exactly one facility and an initial nonnegative limit event; deposits have none. Facility currency equals account currency.
Cards belong only to credit-card accounts. Issue precedes expiry. Assignments begin no earlier than issue; PRIMARY card users must be active primary account owners at assignment start.
A replacement references an older card on the same account; no self-reference or replacement cycle is allowed.

Card activity occurs after issue. Linked authorizations must be approved and use the same card, merchant and currency; multiple presentments are allowed. Refunds have no authorization link in this release.

A REFUND references a PURCHASE on the same card, merchant and currency. A PURCHASE has no original reference. Refund posting does not precede purchase posting; cumulative refunds do not exceed purchase amount.
All transaction, requested, payment, entry and claimed amounts are strictly positive. Money is represented as decimal strings in future JSON records, never binary floating-point values.

CARD entries have only card_transaction_id populated among source references; PAYMENT has only payment_id; FEE has only fee_type_id; ADJUSTMENT has none; REVERSAL has only reverses_entry_id. Non-reversals have no reversal reference.

Each card transaction has exactly one original CARD entry for its card account and equal amount; PURCHASE is DEBIT and REFUND is CREDIT. Each POSTED payment has exactly one original PAYMENT CREDIT entry of equal amount for its receiving account. PENDING or FAILED payments have none.

A reversal points to one non-reversal entry on the same account, has equal amount and opposite direction, and posts no earlier. Each original entry may be reversed at most once; partial reversals are deferred.

Statement lines refer to entries on the statement account within its half-open period. For credit-card statements, closing_balance = opening_balance + debits - credits. Cycles on one account do not overlap; each eligible entry appears exactly once in its issued cycle.

Statements exist only for credit-card accounts. Period start precedes end; issue is on or after period end; due date is after issue; minimum due is nonnegative and no greater than max(closing_balance,0).

Between consecutive daily snapshots, deposit balance changes by credits minus debits; credit-card amount owed changes by debits minus credits. A gap requires all intervening entries. Snapshots may be negative.

A dispute references a PURCHASE; claim does not exceed its amount. Claimant is an account owner or assigned card user at purchase occurrence. Multiple cases may exist, but only one active case per purchase is allowed.

Effective times are unique within each owner stream (consent also by purpose). Initial states are OPEN for accounts, ISSUED for cards and OPEN for disputes; latest event defines current state. Full allowed-transition matrices are deferred.
All currencies are CAD; payment and card activity currency must equal the associated account currency. Payment destination is a credit-card account.
At most one preferred contact exists per customer and contact type.
Closure date is on or after opening and agrees with the CLOSED event business date. Reopening is deferred. UTC instants map to business dates using America/Toronto.
Consent decisions are immutable events. Current consent is the latest decision for the customer and purpose; absence means no recorded grant.

journeys.title: Investigate a disputed purchase
journeys.question: Who used the card, what posted, and what happened to the complaint?

steps.text: Find the customer raising the complaint.
Identify their card assignment at the purchase time.
Keep the original card even if it has since been replaced.
Find the posted purchase rather than an authorization hold.
Read the amount and reason for the claim.

journeys.caveat: The highlighted graph explains joins; it does not prove a claim or automatically credit an account.

journeys.title: Explain a monthly statement
journeys.question: How did purchases, repayments and fees affect the amount owed?

steps.text: Read the billing period and opening balance.
Find the items included in the issued document.
Use booked debits and credits to reconcile the closing balance.
Trace card entries to purchases or refunds.
Trace repayment entries to posted payments.

journeys.caveat: This is a branching explanation, not a single SQL join path. Aggregate entries before joining optional source tables; the statement is not an interest calculator.
